title: Revocation (Experiment 5)
demonstrates: Revoking an artifact or a signing key invalidates it and everything derived from it, and the gateway blocks deployment. Since v0.4 trust and revocation live in a signed, pinned, append-only log: editing the SQLite index (un-revoke, rogue key) and tampering with the log itself (truncate, edit, delete) are all detected and fail closed.

V7 FAIL: revoked ancestor(s): digits-base-cnn

V4 FAIL: trust log unusable (fail closed): record 5 (trust_key): signature by root key invalid - log tampered with
V6 FAIL: parent digits-base-cnn FAILED (V3, V4, V6, V7); parent digits-finetune FAILED (V3, V4, V7)

variants.title: Bypass: delete the trust log
evidence: V3 FAIL: trust log unusable, signer cannot be resolved: trust log missing (trust_log.jsonl); pinned head is #5
V4 FAIL: trust log unusable (fail closed): trust log missing (trust_log.jsonl); pinned head is #5
V6 FAIL: parent digits-base-cnn FAILED (V3, V4, V6, V7); parent digits-finetune FAILED (V3, V4, V7)
V7 FAIL: trust log unusable, revocation state cannot be confirmed: trust log missing (trust_log.jsonl); pinned head is #5

interpretation: Artifact and key revocation propagate to every descendant and block deployment. Every bypass that edits the SQLite index (delete rows, cached status, un-revoke, rogue key) fails because the verifier reads trust and revocation from the signed, pinned trust log, and every attack on the log itself (truncation, in-place edit, deletion) fails closed because the log must replay exactly to the pinned head under the root key's signatures. The v0.3 limitation E5-C4 is closed.
